cvEn:
Eli Hamoi, son of Tzvia and Nisim, was born in 1975 in Tel Aviv.

Eli (Eliyahu Refael Hai) grew up in Tel Aviv and was educated there. After finishing elementary school, he studied at the "Geula" education house and then transferred to the "Shevach" high school (today Shevach Mofet). He completed his studies with great success in the vehicle mechanics track.

Eli was blessed with exceptional respect for his parents. He used to call his mother "my crown," and he was a respectful and loving son to his parents. His attitude toward all his family members was marked by love, devotion and sincere care, and he was a loving and supportive son and brother.

He was a principled and modest person who always preferred deeds to words. Eli treated those around him with respect and friendship, and he believed in the importance of family values, heritage and love of the land.

From childhood he was surrounded by many friends, with whom he loved to play and spend time. Among his friends he was known as someone you could rely on. He knew how to keep a secret, and his friends would consult him and share their personal affairs with him.

Eli always took care with his appearance and liked to wear tailored, neat clothes. But it was not only his outward appearance that was meticulous. He had a big, generous heart, and his generosity was also expressed in the small things of life. For example, when he went out to restaurants with his friends, he would always leave generous tips.

Eli loved sports very much and enjoyed running along the seashore. Another hobby he enjoyed was music. He loved listening to music and invested in acquiring high-quality audio systems and speakers. He also showed great interest in cars.

After completing his high school studies, Eli enlisted in the IDF and served in the Navy as a marine mechanic. He began his service on the ship "Devorah," and afterward was posted to the INS "Meoz," where he served for most of his military service.

Towards the end of his military service, Eli began to feel unwell, and after a series of tests it became clear that he had been stricken with cancer.

Eli was discharged from the army and for five years underwent intensive treatment.

The day before he passed away, his commander from the army visited him in the hospital. When asked what his greatest dream was, Eli replied that it was to sail once more on a ship.

Eli Hamoi passed away on 21 Tishrei 5761 (20 October 2000) at the age of twenty-five. He was laid to rest in the Yarkon Cemetery in Tel Aviv. He left behind his parents, four sisters and three brothers.

His sister Frida wrote: "My dear brother Eli, I have no words to say how great the pain is! How much you are missed in the family picture! There is a great void without you. The years pass and another Memorial Day arrives, as if this were the only day we remember you; every day is a day of remembrance for the family... I miss you, my little brother."

Eli is commemorated on the memorial at the Shevach Mofet high school for students who fell in Israel's wars.
